newsitem.title: USA: Plains cattle markets remain quiet - private.
newsitem.headline: Plains cattle markets remain quiet - private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet Monday afternoon, with feedlot managers saying they were unconcerned about the lack of attention from meat packers.

A few bids of $70.00 to $71.00 per cwt were reported early Monday, but mostly buyers were content to inspect cattle on this week's showlists. Most of the listed cattle were short-fed, many with 100 days or less on feed.
Cattle were priced at $73.00 but sources said bids of $72.00 would result in sales. Sources said a $72.00-price would result in a $75- to $100-per-head profit.

Profitable fed cattle prices coupled with the seasonal movement of feeder cattle off pastures have resulted in active placements recently at High Plains feedlots. Feedlot sources estimated many Kansas to Texas feedlots were filled about 90 percent of capacity.
An Oklahoma source said that normally, placements turn active in October but were active later this year because lush fall pastures allowed cattle to graze longer.
